name: Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet on the floor. Lower the bar to the middle of your chest, then press it back up until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades pulled together and your wrists straight over your elbows.

name: Incline Bench Press
instructions: Set the bench to a 30 to 45 degree angle. Lower the bar to your upper chest and press it back up.
tips: A steeper bench works the shoulders more; stay near 30 degrees to keep the work on the chest.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand over your chest. Lower them to the sides of your chest, then press them up.
tips: Lower slowly. The dumbbells let your elbows travel deeper than a bar does.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
instructions: Sit on a bench set to a slight incline with dumbbells at your shoulders. Press them up and slightly together, then lower with control.
tips: Do not bounce the weights off your shoulders at the bottom.

name: Machine Chest Press
instructions: Sit with your back against the pad and the handles at chest height. Press forward until your arms are straight, then return slowly.
tips: A good first chest exercise: the machine keeps the movement path fixed.

name: Chest Fly
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with dumbbells over your chest and a small bend in your elbows. Open your arms wide in an arc, then bring them back together.
tips: Keep the elbow bend the same all the way; this is a stretch, not a press.

name: Cable Crossover
instructions: Stand between two high pulleys, step forward and lean slightly. Bring the handles down and together in front of your hips, then let them open slowly.
tips: Squeeze for a second where your hands meet.

name: Push-Up
instructions: Start in a plank with your hands under your shoulders. Lower your chest to just above the floor, then push back up with your body in a straight line.
tips: Keep your core tight so your hips do not sag. Do them on your knees if you need to.

name: Chest Dip
instructions: Hold yourself on parallel bars with your arms straight. Lean forward, lower until your upper arms are about level with the floor, then push back up.
tips: Leaning forward shifts the work to the chest; staying upright works the triceps more.

name: Deadlift
instructions: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot. Hinge at the hips, grip the bar and stand up by pushing the floor away, keeping the bar close to your legs. Lower it the same way.
tips: Keep your back flat and the bar touching your legs all the way up and down.

name: Barbell Row
instructions: Hinge forward with a flat back holding the bar. Pull it to your lower ribs, squeeze your shoulder blades, then lower it with control.
tips: Do not use your lower back to swing the weight up.

name: Pull-Up
instructions: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip a little wider than your shoulders. Pull until your chin is over the bar, then lower fully.
tips: Start each rep from a full hang. Use a band or the assisted machine to build up.

name: Chin-Up
instructions: Hang from a bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip. Pull your chin over the bar, then lower slowly.
tips: Easier than a pull-up for most people, and it works the biceps more.

name: Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit with your thighs under the pad and grip the bar wider than your shoulders. Pull it to your upper chest, then let it rise slowly.
tips: Lead with your elbows and do not lean back to yank the bar down.

name: Seated Cable Row
instructions: Sit with your knees slightly bent and a tall chest. Pull the handle to your stomach, squeeze your shoulder blades together, then return slowly.
tips: Keep your torso still; the movement comes from your arms and back.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
instructions: Rest one hand and knee on a bench. Pull the dumbbell from the floor to your hip, then lower it fully.
tips: Think of pulling your elbow to the ceiling rather than lifting the weight with your hand.

name: T-Bar Row
instructions: Straddle the bar and hinge forward with a flat back. Pull the handle to your chest, then lower it with control.
tips: A chest-supported version takes the strain off your lower back.

name: Face Pull
instructions: Set a rope at face height. Pull it towards your face, with your hands ending beside your ears and elbows high, then return slowly.
tips: Good for the rear shoulders and posture. Keep the weight light.

name: Back Extension
instructions: On a back extension bench with your hips at the pad, lower your torso, then raise it until your body is in a straight line.
tips: Stop at a straight line; leaning back further adds stress without benefit.

name: Overhead Press
instructions: Stand with the bar at your collarbone. Press it straight overhead as your head moves slightly forward, then lower it back to your shoulders.
tips: Squeeze your glutes and keep your ribs down so you do not arch your back.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit with dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward. Press them overhead until your arms are straight, then lower with control.
tips: Do not let the dumbbells drift forward of your head.

name: Arnold Press
instructions: Start with dumbbells in front of your chest, palms facing you. Rotate your palms outward as you press overhead, then reverse on the way down.
tips: Move smoothly; the rotation is what makes it different from a normal press.

name: Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides. Raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, then lower slowly.
tips: Use light weights and lead with your elbows, not your hands.

name: Front Raise
instructions: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs. Raise one or both arms straight in front of you to shoulder height, then lower slowly.
tips: Do not swing your body to get the weight up.

name: Rear Delt Fly
instructions: Hinge forward with dumbbells hanging below you. Raise your arms out to the sides until they are level with your back, then lower slowly.
tips: Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.

name: Upright Row
instructions: Hold a bar in front of your thighs with a grip slightly narrower than your shoulders. Pull it up to your chest with your elbows leading, then lower.
tips: Stop at chest height to protect your shoulders.

name: Shrug
instructions: Hold heavy dumbbells at your sides. Lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears, pause, then lower.
tips: Go straight up and down; rolling your shoulders adds nothing.

name: Barbell Curl
instructions: Stand holding a bar with an underhand grip. Curl it up to your chest keeping your elbows by your sides, then lower slowly.
tips: Do not swing your back to start the lift.

name: Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand. Curl them up, turning your palms up as you lift, then lower with control.
tips: Alternate arms if it helps you keep your form.

name: Hammer Curl
instructions: Hold dumbbells with your palms facing each other. Curl them up without turning your wrists, then lower slowly.
tips: Also works the forearms and the muscle beneath the biceps.

name: Preacher Curl
instructions: Rest your upper arms on the preacher pad. Curl the bar up, then lower it until your arms are almost straight.
tips: Do not let the bar drop at the bottom.

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Sit back on an incline bench with your arms hanging. Curl the dumbbells up, then lower fully to stretch the biceps.
tips: The incline puts your arms behind your body for a deeper stretch.

name: Cable Curl
instructions: Stand facing a low pulley with a straight bar. Curl it up with your elbows still, then lower slowly.
tips: The cable keeps tension on the muscle through the whole movement.

name: Tricep Pushdown
instructions: Stand at a high pulley with an overhand grip. Keep your elbows by your sides and push the bar down until your arms are straight, then let it rise.
tips: Only your forearms move.

name: Skull Crusher
instructions: Lie on a bench with a bar over your chest. Bend your elbows to lower it towards your forehead, then extend your arms.
tips: Keep your upper arms still and pointing at the ceiling.

name: Overhead Tricep Extension
instructions: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands. Lower it behind your head by bending your elbows, then extend your arms.
tips: Keep your elbows pointing forward, not flaring out.

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
instructions: Lie on a bench and grip the bar with your hands about shoulder width apart. Lower it to your lower chest and press up.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your body.

name: Bench Dip
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench with your hands beside your hips and your legs out. Slide forward and lower your body by bending your elbows, then push back up.
tips: Bend your knees to make it easier.

name: Tricep Kickback
instructions: Hinge forward with your upper arm parallel to the floor. Extend your forearm back until your arm is straight, then return.
tips: Light weight and a pause at the top works better than a heavy swing.

name: Squat
instructions: Place the bar across your upper back. Sit down and back until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then stand up.
tips: Keep your knees in line with your toes and your chest up.

name: Front Squat
instructions: Rest the bar on the front of your shoulders with your elbows high. Squat down keeping your torso upright, then stand.
tips: The front load makes you stay tall and works the quads hard.

name: Goblet Squat
instructions: Hold one dumbbell at your chest. Squat down between your knees, then stand back up.
tips: A friendly way to learn the squat pattern.

name: Leg Press
instructions: Sit in the machine with your feet shoulder width apart on the platform. Lower the platform until your knees are at about 90 degrees, then press it away.
tips: Do not lock your knees at the top or let your lower back lift off the pad.

name: Hack Squat
instructions: Stand on the platform with your back on the pad. Lower until your thighs are parallel to it, then push back up.
tips: Feet lower on the platform works the quads; higher works the glutes more.

name: Lunge
instructions: Step forward and lower your back knee towards the floor. Push through your front foot to return to standing, then switch legs.
tips: Keep your front knee over your ankle and your torso upright.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: Rest your back foot on a bench behind you. Lower your back knee towards the floor, then stand up on your front leg.
tips: Take a long enough step that your front shin stays upright.

name: Step-Up
instructions: Place one foot on a bench or box. Push through that foot to stand on top, then step back down with control.
tips: Do not push off with the back foot.

name: Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand holding a bar at your thighs. Push your hips back, lowering the bar down your legs until you feel a stretch behind your thighs, then stand up.
tips: Keep your knees slightly bent and your back flat.

name: Leg Extension
instructions: Sit with the pad on your lower shins. Straighten your legs, pause, then lower slowly.
tips: Do not swing the weight up with momentum.

name: Leg Curl
instructions: Lie or sit in the machine with the pad above your heels. Bend your knees to curl the pad towards you, then return slowly.
tips: Keep your hips down on the pad.

name: Calf Raise
instructions: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step and the weight on your shoulders. Rise onto your toes, pause, then lower below the step.
tips: Use the full range of movement and pause at the top.

name: Seated Calf Raise
instructions: Sit with the pad on your thighs and the balls of your feet on the platform. Raise your heels, pause, then lower fully.
tips: The bent knee works the deeper calf muscle.

name: Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit with your upper back against a bench and a bar across your hips. Drive your hips up until your body is in a straight line, squeeze, then lower.
tips: Tuck your chin and look forward; do not arch your lower back at the top.

name: Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent. Push through your heels to lift your hips until your body is straight, then lower.
tips: Squeeze your glutes at the top for a second.

name: Cable Kickback
instructions: Attach a strap to your ankle at a low pulley. Kick your leg straight back, squeeze, then return slowly.
tips: Keep your hips square and do not arch your back.

name: Sumo Deadlift
instructions: Stand with a wide stance and toes turned out, gripping the bar inside your knees. Stand up by pushing the floor apart, then lower with control.
tips: Keep your knees tracking over your toes.

name: Plank
instructions: Rest on your forearms and toes with your body in a straight line. Hold the position with your core tight.
tips: Hold for 30 to 60 seconds per set. Do not let your hips sag or rise.

name: Side Plank
instructions: Lie on your side and prop yourself on your forearm. Lift your hips so your body is in a straight line and hold.
tips: Hold for 20 to 45 seconds each side.

name: Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent. Curl your shoulders off the floor towards your hips, then lower slowly.
tips: Keep your neck relaxed; the movement comes from your abs.

name: Bicycle Crunch
instructions: Lie on your back with your hands by your head. Bring one elbow towards the opposite knee as you straighten the other leg, then switch.
tips: Slow and controlled beats fast.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
instructions: Hang from a bar. Raise your legs straight up in front of you, then lower them slowly without swinging.
tips: Bend your knees to make it easier.

name: Russian Twist
instructions: Sit leaning back slightly with your feet off the floor. Rotate your torso from side to side, touching the floor beside you.
tips: Hold a weight to make it harder.

name: Cable Crunch
instructions: Kneel below a high pulley holding the rope at your head. Curl your torso down, bringing your elbows towards your knees, then return slowly.
tips: Move through your spine, not your hips.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
instructions: Kneel holding an ab wheel under your shoulders. Roll forward as far as you can keep your back flat, then pull back.
tips: Stop before your lower back starts to sag.

name: Mountain Climber
instructions: Start in a push-up position. Drive one knee towards your chest, then switch legs quickly.
tips: Keep your hips low and your core tight.

name: Treadmill Run
instructions: Run or walk at a pace you can keep up. Warm up for a few minutes first and cool down at the end.
tips: Track your time rather than reps; one set is the whole session.

name: Rowing Machine
instructions: Push with your legs first, then lean back and pull the handle to your lower ribs. Return in the reverse order.
tips: The power comes mostly from your legs.

name: Cycling
instructions: Pedal at a steady effort on a stationary bike or outdoors. Adjust the seat so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom.
tips: Easy on the joints, good for recovery days.

name: Jump Rope
instructions: Turn the rope with your wrists and jump just high enough to clear it, landing softly on the balls of your feet.
tips: Start with short rounds and build up.

name: Burpee
instructions: From standing, drop to a push-up position, do a push-up, jump your feet back in and jump up with your arms overhead.
tips: Pace yourself; the first few rounds should feel easy.

name: Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Hinge at the hips with the kettlebell between your legs. Snap your hips forward to swing it to chest height, then let it swing back.
tips: It is a hip hinge, not a squat or a front raise.

name: Clean and Press
instructions: Pull the bar from the floor to your shoulders in one movement, then press it overhead. Lower it back to your shoulders and to the floor.
tips: Learn each part separately with a light bar first.

name: Thruster
instructions: Hold dumbbells at your shoulders. Squat down, and as you stand up press the weights overhead in one smooth movement.
tips: Use the power of your legs to drive the press.

name: Farmer's Walk
instructions: Pick up a heavy dumbbell in each hand and walk with tall posture and short steps for about 30 metres.
tips: A great test of grip, core and posture.
